description: Robo's race car needs fuel: add 27 + 15! Trade 10 ones for 1 ten at Pig's Trade Booth, fix Robo's 312 crash, and subtract with regrouping on the reverse lap.

youtube.title: Regroup Rally! 2-Digit Addition and Subtraction with Regrouping | Grade 2 Math | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Robo's race car will only start if we add 27 + 15. At Pig's Trade Booth, 10 ones go in and 1 ten comes out: that's regrouping!
We fix Robo's 312 crash by estimating, race through 38 + 46 and 59 + 23, then subtract with trading on the reverse lap (52 - 17, 63 - 28) and check by adding back.
Try at home: 46 + 18 and 50 - 23 with pasta or blocks.

do.text: Regroup Rally
Welcome to the Regroup Rally! My remote car is ready.
Woof! My blue car is ready too.
Three, two, one... go!
Oh no! My car won't start. The screen says...
Add 27 plus 15 to unlock the fuel!
The other car is already moving. Quick, let's think!
Let's warm up with an easier one first. 34 plus 25.
Rule one of the rally: always start with the ones.
ones
Here are 34 and 25 as blocks.
Tens are tall rods. Ones are little cubes.
Ones first. 4 plus 5 is 9.
Nine cubes. That's fine, nine fits in the ones place.
But why start with the ones and not the tens?
If the ones make ten or more, the tens get a new ten!
Now the tens. 3 tens plus 2 tens is 5 tens.
34 plus 25 is 59. No trade needed!
Easy. Now for the real fuel puzzle.
Back to 27 plus 15.
27 is 2 tens and 7 ones.
15 is 1 ten and 5 ones.
Ones first. 7 plus 5 is...?
12! Count the cubes with me.
But 12 can't fit in the ones place. It's two digits!
Right! Only 0 to 9 fit in a place.
0 to 9
So when we have 10 ones, we go to the Trade Booth!
Oink! Ten ones in, one ten out!
When I say ten ones, you say trade for a ten!
Ten ones!
Trade for a ten! Great!
We traded 10 ones for 1 ten. That's called regrouping.
regroup
2 ones stay in the ones place. Write 2.
The new ten rides up to the tens. We carry the 1.
Now the tens. 2 plus 1, plus the carried 1, makes 4.
4 tens and 2 ones. 27 plus 15 is 42!
But why do we carry the 1? Why not keep 12 ones?
Because 10 ones is the same as 1 ten.
Same amount, new shape.
Fun fact: we use only ten digits,
0 to 9. So we trade at ten!
Fuel unlocked!
Wait, let me write it my way first. 7 plus 5 is 12.
I write 12 under the ones, then 3 for the tens.
So the answer is 312!
Too big! 27 is less than 30, and 15 is less than 20.
So the answer must be less than 50. 312 is way too big.
You're right. I put the whole 12 in the ones place.
Only the 2 stays. The 10 goes to the tens as 1 ten.
Estimate first. About 30 plus 15 is 45. 42 is close. Good.
Hands on your wheels, everyone! Steer to checkpoint 2!
Checkpoint 2! 38 plus 46.
Ones first. 8 plus 6 is...?
14! Do we need a trade?
Yes! 14 is 10 ones and 4 more. Write 4, carry 1 ten.
Hold on. Why do we carry a 1, and not a 10?
The 1 sits in the tens place, so it means 1 ten. That's 10!
Tens: 3 plus 4 plus the carried 1 is 8.
38 plus 46 is 84!
Check: about 40 plus 45 is 85. 84 is close. Yes.
Checkpoint 3! 59 plus 23.
Can I do the ones? 9 plus 3 is...?
12! Ten ones go to the Trade Booth. Write 2, carry 1.
Tens: 5 plus 2 plus 1 is 8.
59 plus 23 is 82!
Check: about 60 plus 20 is 80. 82 is close. Good driving.
Three checkpoints done. Remember:
start with the ones every time!
Drive with your hands on the wheel and chant with me!
Vroom! Ten in the ones? Pit stop, swap!
One ten up to the top!
Vroom! Ten in the ones? Pit stop, swap!
One ten up to the top!
Ones go first, tens go next. Carry the ten, you're the best!
Now the reverse lap! We give fuel away. 52 take away 17.
52 is 5 tens and 2 ones.
Ones first. 2 take away 7?
You can't take 7 cubes from 2 cubes.
There are not enough ones here, so we trade.
Open one ten into 10 ones at the Trade Booth!
It's still 52. Just a new shape: 4 tens and 12 ones.
This trade is regrouping too. Some people call it borrowing.
regroup
Now 12 take away 7 is 5. Write 5.
Tens: 4 take away 1 is 3. Write 3.
52 take away 17 is 35!
Fun fact: you can always check a take-away by adding back.
35 plus 17. 5 plus 7 is 12, carry 1. 3 plus 1 plus 1 is 5.
52! It matches, so 35 is right!
Your turn. 63 take away 28.
Ones first. 3 take away 8. Do we trade?
Yes! 6 tens become 5 tens and 13 ones.
13 take away 8 is 5. Then 5 take away 2 is 3.
63 take away 28 is 35.
Check: 35 plus 28 is 63. Yes!
Look! Both answers were 35. Different problems, same answer!
When there are not enough ones, we trade a ten. Got it!
Final lap! Three problems against the clock.
You get five seconds to think each time. Ready?
First: 68 plus 27. Ones first!
8 plus 7 is 15. Write 5, carry 1.
6 plus 2 plus 1 is 9. 95!
About 70 plus 25 is 95. Spot on.
Next: 71 take away 34.
1 take away 4? Trade! 11 take away 4 is 7.
6 take away 3 is 3. The answer is 37.
Check: 37 plus 34 is 71. Yes.
Last one: 40 take away 16.
0 take away 6? Trade! 10 take away 6 is 4.
3 take away 1 is 2. The answer is 24!
Check: 24 plus 16 is 40. We did it!
Finish line!
To the podium! Then a quick quiz.
46 plus 37 is...?
83! 6 plus 7 is 13. Write 3, carry 1. 4 plus 3 plus 1 is 8.
54 take away 29 is...?
25! 14 take away 9 is 5. 4 take away 2 is 2.
Why do we trade 10 ones?
10 ones make 1 ten, and only 0 to 9 fit in the ones place.
Is 35 plus 17 a good check for 52 take away 17?
Yes! Adding back gives 52.
Everyone wins the Regroup Rally!
Try 46 plus 18 at home with pasta pieces. Bye!
